source.title: On the Origin of Implicit Regularization in Stochastic Gradient Descent
source.authors: Samuel L. Smith; Benoit Dherin; D. G. Barrett; Soham De

record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and learning-rate or regularization scaling and reports test accuracy, addressing when batch size changes the generalization outcome.
record.gate_note: The study also reports learning-rate and explicit-regularizer effects, plus n-step SGD results; those do not directly test a listed version and are recorded under fits_no_version. Results cited from prior work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study varies batch size and measures held-out accuracy, testing V5's provision that adapting learning rates or regularization can preserve accuracy. It is not an original source for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors derive a first-order modified loss for the mean SGD iterate under shuffled, non-overlapping minibatches and small finite learning rates. Explicitly adding its gradient-norm penalty can improve test accuracy. Their n-step experiments argue against SDE temperature alone explaining generalization. They leave open whether higher-order or oscillatory effects also contribute.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies batch size and learning-rate or regularization scaling and measures test accuracy, but does not reproduce the fixed-recipe large-batch comparisons in V5. It also studies implicit regularization and n-step SGD.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with learning rate, explicit regularization strength, batch size, and n-step SGD setting; the batch-size trend depends on holding ε/B or λ/B constant. The authors note that the ε/B relationship breaks down for very large batch sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Explicitly adding the minibatch-gradient-norm regularizer improves late-training CIFAR-10 test accuracy at a small learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A minibatch-gradient-norm penalty can improve held-out accuracy in this Wide-ResNet setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Test accuracy varies non-monotonically with learning rate and regularization strength; explicit regularization brings the training- and test-optimal learning rates together.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite learning rates can confer a generalization benefit that an explicit gradient-norm penalty partly reproduces.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing repeated updates per minibatch lowers optimized CIFAR-10 accuracy, whereas Fashion-MNIST accuracy remains similar at matched bare learning rates or independently optimized settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization under repeated minibatch updates depends on bare learning rate and workload, and is not explained solely by effective-learning-rate-based SDE temperature.

record.problems: The paper states that the analysis assumes mε is small, an extreme approximation when N/B is large, and that higher-order terms may matter at practical learning rates. Experiments are limited to the reported model and dataset settings; test-accuracy comparisons are often described through figures without exact per-condition values. The authors note finite compute and possible incomplete convergence, especially at small learning rates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible claim-related results were omitted. Figure-only trends are included when the text explicitly describes the outcome; exact values are not inferred from plots.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding natural- versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Generalization as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.

The fixed-recipe penalty beyond an identified workload-dependent batch threshold; language models; warmup and normalization interventions; isolated regularization recovery at equal epochs. Very-large-batch breakdown of regularization scaling is predicted but explicitly not experimentally tested.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Only supplied text was used. Similar accuracy after adaptation is evidence for V5's adaptation provision, not a challenge to its fixed-recipe penalty. States for rows linked to none are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; their reported findings can still be valid. Very-large-batch predictions are not observed results. Selected best runs and, where specified, peak test checkpoints limit interpretation of the reported accuracy summaries.

versions.untested_parts: The fixed-recipe large-batch penalty across image classifiers and language models; normalization or regularization changes; same-epoch comparisons beyond the reported settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

rows.subject: 10-1 Wide-ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Varied batch size and learning rate while training on the original loss; compared test accuracies at fixed learning-rate-to-batch-size ratios.

conditions.value: ε/B constant; batch size not too large

rows.value: Different batch sizes achieve similar test accuracies if the ratio ε/B is constant and B is not too large.
rows.uncertainty: Mean test accuracy; uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The text describes the pattern but supplies no per-batch numerical values.
rows.check: The reported equality supports V5's recipe-adaptation provision, rather than indicating a partial effect. The comparison holds epochs fixed at 6400 and scales learning rate with batch size; it applies only when batch size is not too large.

rows.subject: 10-1 Wide-ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Varied batch size and explicit regularization coefficient while training on the modified loss; compared test accuracies at fixed regularization-coefficient-to-batch-size ratios.
rows.value: Different batch sizes achieve similar test accuracy so long as the ratio λ/B is constant.
rows.note: The text describes similar accuracy and notes that the pattern is expected to break down for very large batch sizes; numerical values are not given.
rows.check: Equality supports the adaptation provision under combined changes to regularization and training exposure. Holding 10 million updates fixed gives larger batches more epochs, so this does not isolate regularization scaling or demonstrate same-epoch recovery.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 Wide-ResNet at 6400 epochs and Fashion-MNIST MLP at 400 epochs, with learning rate scaled proportionally to batch size
relationships.reason: R1 and R3 report similar held-out accuracy across batch sizes at constant learning-rate-to-batch-size ratio, supporting same-epoch preservation through recipe adaptation within the tested range.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports similar accuracy across batches at a constant learning-rate-to-batch-size ratio, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 Wide-ResNet with proportional regularization scaling and 10 million updates
relationships.reason: R2 reports similar accuracy across batch sizes under this combined adaptation; larger batches also receive more epochs, so the result does not identify regularization scaling alone as sufficient.
relationships.display_finding: Combined regularization scaling and fixed-update training reportedly preserved accuracy, but the comparison remains unverified and larger batches received more epochs.

relationships.condition: Fashion-MNIST MLP with proportional regularization scaling and 1.5 million updates
relationships.reason: R4 reports slightly higher accuracy for smaller batches despite matched regularization-to-batch-size ratios and more epochs for larger batches, qualifying complete batch-size equivalence under this recipe.
relationships.display_finding: The reported small-batch accuracy advantage despite matched regularization-to-batch-size ratios and longer large-batch training remains unverified.
